subject.title: [Bug]: read tool drops memory/ prefix in multi-agent setup, causing ENOENT

question: Should maintainers accept PR https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96453's scoped read-tool fallback for bare daily-memory filenames, or require the prefix-loss fix upstream in startup/context generation?
rationale: The issue is valid at the read-tool boundary and has a focused candidate fix, but the candidate intentionally changes behavior for missing bare `YYYY-MM-DD.md` reads after ENOENT, so maintainer intent should settle the permanent boundary.

options.title: Accept scoped fallback
options.body: Land the open PR if normal checks stay green and keep the synthesized retry sandbox guard intact.

options.title: Move fix upstream
options.body: Ask for a revised PR that prevents the model from losing `memory/` before the read-tool boundary instead of adding fallback inference there.

options.title: Wait for more live proof
options.body: Keep the issue and PR open until a maintainer obtains a fresh current-main multi-agent heartbeat/inbound repro.

recommendation.title: Accept scoped fallback
recommendation.body: Land the open PR if normal checks stay green and keep the synthesized retry sandbox guard intact.

likelyOwner.reason: The open decision centers on the agent read-tool boundary and fallback semantics where Vincent Koc has recent adjacent history.
